newsitem.title: USA: CME seeks amendments to live cattle delivery rules.
newsitem.headline: CME seeks amendments to live cattle delivery rules.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange is planning to add provisions for sub-standard cattle to be delivered against live cattle futures, a CME release stated.

The CME's Board of Directors on Wednesday approved amendments to proposed Live Cattle delivery rules which will take effect for newly-listed contracts upon Commodity Futures Trading Commission approval.
The planned change will add a category for cattle that grade below Standard. Such cattle will be discounted an amount equal to the Standard grade discount plus 25 percent of the settlement price.

Without the penalty, under certain market conditions, delivering shorts might find it economically profitable to deliver full loads of cattle grading Commercial and below against the contract, according to the release.

The rules changes also specify that quality grade adjustments for all delivery units will make use of the live weight equivalent of the Choice-Select boxed beef spread calculated from information reported by U.S. Department of Agriculture for the day of tender in its National Carlot Meat Report. In addition, quality grade, yield grade and carcass weight adjustments will include factors calculated from values reported by USDA in the National Carcass Premiums and Discounts for Slaughter Steers and Heifers report.
